meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (Registro Mercantil Central and Notarial District of the registered office)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain-United States Income Tax Convention (1990, in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (as amended by Real Decreto-ley 11/2018); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, de desarrollo reglamentario; Real Decreto 95/2024, de 16 de enero, por el que se regula el Registro de Titularidades Reales; corporate law basis: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified copy of registered details of the corporate shareholder, including articles of association, registry extract and certificate of incumbency
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry in the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961); Consular Legalization for non-Hague member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostilled passport copy and NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) application record for each individual shareholder, director and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the country of origin and Spanish Consular Office for NIE issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille combined with sworn translation into Spanish by a certified translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and certificate of account titleholder (certificado de titularidad) for the purpose of source-of-funds verification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The shareholder's banking institution in the EU or third country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille and certified Spanish translation for third-country banks

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Statutory declaration of the final UBO chain and economic rationale of the Spanish SL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: To be signed before the Spanish notary at the date of the incorporation deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial act embedded in the escritura pública de constitución

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, authorized signatories and UBOs against (i) the Spanish jurisdictional PEP lists derived from BOE public appointments, (ii) the OFAC SDN List, (iii) United Nations consolidated lists, and (iv) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, which incorporates Council Implementing Regulations applicable in Spain. The screening must be executed before the notarial deed is granted and repeated at least annually; simplified due diligence is permitted for the Low_Risk_Standard ISIC 6201 helpdesk/SaaS profile but never waives UBO identification, the bank reference requirement, or adverse-media verification.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) online denomination certification service, accessible at https://www.registradores.org and through the RMC Sede Electrónica (certificación negativa de denominación)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate denominations must be drafted in Spanish or Spanish-compatible Latin characters; if a foreign word is used, it must be transcribed in the statutory Spanish spelling and must not conflict with Spanish orthographic rules. The approved denomination contained in the certification must be reproduced with absolute fidelity in the notarial deed and registration application; neither translation nor transliteration is permitted after certification.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España or Spanish official emblems and coat-of-arms
Ministerio, Consejo, Gobierno, Real (in a manner suggesting royal or governmental status)
Banco, Caja, Ahorro, Aseguradora, Reaseguradora, Mutualidad (regulated financial-sector tokens requiring prior supervisor approval)
Comunidad Autónoma, Ayuntamiento, Diputación (official territorial denominations)
Sociedad Anónima, S.A., S.L. or any corporate type token inconsistent with the SL form
International, Mundial, Extremo, plus any superlative expression implying false geographical or scale claims (subject to Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública discretionary assessment)
Tokens contrary to law, public order or morality, or likely to mislead third parties
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Mercantil Central rejects a proposed name, the applicant may: (1) file a reconsideration petition (recurso potestativo de reposición) with the Registro Mercantil Central within one month from notification of the rejection; (2) alternatively, file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública of the Ministry of Justice within one month; the appeal must attach a reformulated denomination together with the RMC tariff receipt. The six-month validity of a granted denomination certificate is strictly non-renewable, so upon expiry a fresh application must be submitted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional permissibility. A second-generation virtual office offering a physical address in Spain, staffed reception during business hours and a genuine work-desk facility may satisfy the registered office (domicilio social) mandate provided the company can evidence the helpdesk/SaaS management activity from that location and formally register the domicilio fiscal with Agencia Tributaria (AEAT). Pure mail-forwarding, PO-Box services and unstaffed addresses are legally insufficient and will trigger administrative correction.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 10-15% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection during the first three years, with the higher probability concentrated on AEAT domicilio fiscal verification and Mercantile Registry postal notifications following the opening of an independent corporate bank account receiving Stripe and PayPal settlement funds into a Spanish IBAN. The inspection likelihood rises to approximately 20% if annual accounts are filed late, a registered-office change occurs within the first year, or the company exhibits a commanding-officer pattern inconsistent with the declared helpdesk/SaaS substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory arancel notarial (notarial tariff regulation, Decree applied by Ministerio de Justicia)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mercantile Registry registration filing for the SL and inscription of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Provincial Registro Mercantil with territorial jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) processing and consular appointment for each non-resident shareholder/director
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Consular Office / Oficina de Extranjería

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and sworn Spanish translation of foreign corporate documents and passports
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of origin country / sworn translator registered with Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention member-state tariff and prevailing sworn-translation market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legalization and consular authentication fees for non-Hague signatory country documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register filing and compliance attestation under Real Decreto 95/2024, including preparation of the titularidad real declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for corporate compliance legal assistance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Virtual registered office subscription for the first year, including physical address and reception services
Notarial testimonio copies of the incorporation deed for corporate bank account opening with Stripe/PayPal settlement banking partner

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 19-23 (formation deed and bylaws), Articles 58-62 (capital contributions), Articles 210-214 (administration), and Articles 282-283 (registration and publication effects). Royal Decree 1784/1996, approving the Mercantile Registry Regulations, also applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) for name clearance and the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for registration of the company and its directors.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), accompanied by the corporate bylaws, followed by electronic or physical filing with the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry. The beneficial ownership declaration and tax identification filings must also be completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum share capital of an Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1. The capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. Until share capital reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve until the reserve plus capital reaches EUR 3,000, and shareholders have supplementary liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital upon liquidation if company assets are insufficient. Spain does not generally require a statutory capital escrow account; cash contributions may be evidenced by a bank certificate or by an equivalent founder declaration permitted by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that the Company accept and ratify the subscription and full payment of its issued share capital as stated in the incorporation deed and allot the corresponding quotas to the subscribers. The Board adopts the registered office at the address recorded in the deed and authorizes its use for tax, registry, banking, and official correspondence. The Board appoints the persons identified in the deed as managing director or joint and several directors, as applicable, and authorizes them to obtain the NIF, open bank accounts, execute commercial contracts, and complete all tax, employment, data-protection, and municipal registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), through its online name-certification service or authorized filing channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names, in priority order, together with the applicant identification and payment details. Obtain the negative name certificate. The certificate is generally valid for three months for execution of the deed and has a longer reservation period for registry purposes under the applicable rules. Ensure the proposed name includes the legal form or its accepted abbreviation, S.L.
required_dossiers: Five proposed corporate names, if available
Power of attorney, where filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected, submit an alternative name or correct the identified similarity or legal-form issue. If the certificate expires, request a new certificate before signing the incorporation deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Incorporation Documents and Beneficial Ownership Information
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notarial office selected for execution of the incorporation deed; tax authority procedures may be completed through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the bylaws, capital allocation, registered office evidence, corporate purpose, management structure, director acceptance, identification numbers, and beneficial ownership statement. Obtain Spanish tax identification numbers for non-resident shareholders and directors where required. Arrange sworn translations and apostilles or legalization for foreign documents.
required_dossiers: Founders' passports or national identity documents
Foreign shareholder corporate certificates and powers of attorney, if applicable
Spanish or foreign tax identification numbers
Registered office title, lease, or authorization
Capital contribution evidence or legally permitted founder declaration
Powers of attorney and apostilles or legalization, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure missing legalization, translation, identification, or beneficial ownership information before the notarial appointment. Replace defective powers of attorney and obtain a new corporate certificate where validity or authority is questioned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders or duly authorized attorneys execute the public deed. The notary verifies identity, capacity, name certificate, capital subscription, bylaws, beneficial ownership, and foreign-document formalities. Request the provisional tax identification number and authorize electronic transmission to the Mercantile Registry where available.
required_dossiers: Capital contribution evidence or permitted declaration
Foreign-document translations and apostilles, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect, amend the draft, provide missing evidence, or execute a corrective deed. Do not submit an incomplete deed to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Identification and Register the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria for the NIF; competent Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the provisional NIF using the incorporation deed and Form 036 or the applicable electronic procedure. File the notarised deed electronically with the Provincial Mercantile Registry covering the registered office. After registration, obtain the definitive NIF and update tax records. Complete the legalisation of mandatory electronic corporate books through the Mercantile Registry within the statutory deadlines.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a registry qualification notice by correcting the deed, bylaws, identification, name, capital, or director information. Submit a corrective deed or supplementary document within the stated cure period and refile for review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Governance, Municipal, and Operational Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Relevant Ayuntamiento (municipality), Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social, and applicable autonomous-community authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first board or sole-director resolutions, open the corporate bank account, confirm accounting and invoicing systems, register employers before hiring, and enroll employees with Social Security. Submit any municipal declaration of responsible activity or opening notice required for the registered premises. Register or document data-processing compliance and appoint a representative where required.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or sole-director decision
Municipal responsible declaration or opening filing, if applicable
Social Security registration documents, if hiring
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct municipal or tax filings following an administrative request. If premises activity is queried, provide lease, floor plans, accessibility and fire documentation, or amend the activity classification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board is ordinarily required for a cloud-based helpdesk, SaaS, or conversational-bot business without manufacturing, telecommunications-network operation, or regulated infrastructure. Where premises or equipment fall within an industrial-regulatory category, the competent authority is the Industry department of the relevant Autonomous Community, coordinated nationally by the Ministry of Industry and Tourism.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No national manufacturing or industrial operating permit is ordinarily required. A municipal responsible declaration for opening or activity (declaración responsable de actividad o apertura) may be required for physical premises, depending on the municipality and premises characteristics.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico), together with the competent environmental authority of the relevant Autonomous Community
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from project-level EIA for ordinary office-based SaaS and customer-support operations, absent a qualifying construction, data-centre, industrial, or infrastructure project. A separate screening may apply to construction or material expansion of a data centre.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No sector-specific industrial wastewater or VOC limits ordinarily apply to office-based operations. Comply with municipal sewer-discharge rules where wastewater is discharged, separate and transfer commercial or electronic waste through authorized waste operators, and comply with applicable waste, refrigerant, battery, and electrical-equipment rules. Data-centre operators must separately assess permits for generators, cooling systems, noise, air emissions, and hazardous waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For ordinary office premises, obtain any municipal opening or responsible-activity filing and maintain applicable fire-safety measures under Royal Decree 513/2017 and the Building Code. Structural-load certification is required only where premises alterations, server installations, or equipment loads warrant it. Comply with the Occupational Risk Prevention Act, including risk assessment, emergency planning, worker information, and health and safety arrangements. No separate industrial civil-defense clearance is ordinarily required for a non-industrial helpdesk office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and its official portal at www.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spanish resident entities such as SL obtain NIF automatically upon registration with the Commercial Registry. Non-resident foreign entities must apply for a NIF by submitting incorporation documents, passport, and proof of address via the AEAT online portal or at a tax office; processing takes 10-15 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box elections; however, hybrid mismatch relief elections are available under EU ATAD rules and Spanish tax treaty provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 50,000 EUR annual turnover threshold for mandatory VAT registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered taxpayers must issue electronic invoices with QR codes and report real-time to AEAT via the integrated digital platform. Large enterprises require API connectivity for automated clearance and stamping.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT rate upon proof of export; offshore services to non-EU customers are zero-rated where place of supply rules apply. SaaS helpdesk services provided to non-residents may qualify if not deemed supplied in Spain.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Issuance of fraudulent zero-rated invoices results in fines equivalent to 100% of evaded tax, criminal prosecution, and clawback of undue VAT credits with interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) as the competent monetary authority; exchange control and foreign investment reporting are jointly administered by the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCIIN) of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business, and by the Balance of Payments Department of Banco de España.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Capital and current account transactions are fully liberalised under the EU Treaty and Spanish Royal Decree 1816/1991, subject to statistical notification and anti-money-laundering controls. There is no general permit requirement for inbound equity contributions or outbound profit remittances for a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. However, dividend distribution is blocked until annual accounts are approved and legal reserves are completed, and any remittance to an entity within a non-cooperative jurisdiction is subject to enhanced due diligence. The euro is freely convertible within the eurozone; conversion delays arise only for flows from highly restricted non-convertible currencies where tiered correspondent banking and sanctions screening force temporal queues.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain does not impose any mandatory export proceeds surrender ratio or statutory conversion timeline for export receipts. Exporters may retain all proceeds in EUR or foreign currency accounts both within Spain and abroad. Nevertheless, the Balance of Payments reporting administrative regulation requires residents to file statistical declarations with Banco de España when aggregate foreign currency balances or related annual transfers exceed the applicable thresholds (generally EUR 50,000 month-end balance or EUR 1,000,000 annual cumulative movements).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. EU-pasported electronic money institutions may provide cross-border operational IBAN accounts for UK/EEA-style SaaS businesses without requiring a local Spanish office. Such EMIs are viable for daily collections and payment card settlements, but they are not regarded by legal counsel as
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.viable for statutory capital escrow, com: Medium. EU-pasported electronic money institutions may provide cross-border operational IBAN accounts for tech/SaaS businesses without a local Spanish office. Such EMIs are viable for daily subscription collections and payment card settlements, but they are not regarded as fully bank-grade for fiduciary or escrow use in Spain. Spanish AML Law 10/2010 and PSD2 require that the EMI serves only as a payment institution, not as a full credit institution. Therefore, for an operational helpdesk SaaS treasury, viability is appropriate; for high-value capital landing or escrow custody of statutory funds, viability is low. Final rating - Medium (Operational), Low (Escrow).
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance is ordinarily required for non-resident directors, non-EU beneficial owners, and the appointed legal representative when opening bank accounts under strict Spanish AML protocol. Spanish tier-1 banks do accept remote video-identification through state approved biometric NIA-certified tools for EU-national directors at natural person level, but most institutions reserve the right to require physical presence for the company's representatives if any material beneficial owner is subject to PEP status, sanction screening, or non-EU residence. For a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada at least one managing director or legal representative must appear physically to sign the corporate mandate and complete personal identification unless the bank explicitly permits remote notarised appointments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owners located in high-risk third jurisdictions or FATF-listed/ non-cooperative tax jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified true copies of valid passports and NIE/TIE cards; personal declaration of funds; three months source-of-wealth bank statements; opening bank reference letter; Spanish company deed from notary; full corporate registry certificate (certificado literal del Registro Mercantil); audited financial statements or pro forma balance sheet; and a written business purpose memo linked to the helpdesk subscription contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder or legal representative identified as a politically exposed person (PEP) or bearing potential sanctions flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete PEP scrutiny declaration; transcript from official OFAC/EU sanctions screening system; legal opinion explaining the commercial logic of proposed inflows; notarized authorization to represent the company; passport and NIE copies; and a sworn statement of any previous in-person interview at the bank branch to confirm identity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient local economic substance or remote-only cloud operation with little Spanish physical footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current lease agreement or Spanish virtual office contract; Spanish payroll or NICA registration of at least one local employee; quarterly VAT (modelo 303) and annual corporate income tax receipt; an explanation of the digital cloud architecture and data flow; and an organisation chart evidencing Spanish administrative decision-making responsibilities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border flows from high-risk correspondent banks, payment processors, or crypto-adjacent fiat exchanges
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original customer invoices; valid MT103/MT202 and sender reference copies; the underlying SaaS subscription agreements between the Spanish SL and end-clients; Platform/Contractor confirmation from Stripe and PayPal (if used); and a treasury policy memo delineating permitted inbound channels and the final-use compliance manual.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocol is SWIFT MT103 to the SL's EUR IBAN account using a valid IBAN in Spain, BIC/SWIFT code of the receiving Spanish bank, and a precise purpose code corresponding to 'equity subscription', 'cash capital contribution', or 'shareholder loan'. The beneficiary must be the company (nombre de la empresa) with its Spanish NIF/CIF, and the transfer must clearly state the notarial deed number and inscription date to satisfy the Foreign Investment Registry. If the inbound amount exceeds EUR 3,000,000, a post-closing declaration of foreign investment must be filed with the Registro de Inversores Exteriores of the Ministry of Economy within one month after the contribution. No prior Banco de España clearance is required, but the transfer must not originate from Russia, Belarus, or sanctioned financial intermediaries under EU Regulation 833/2014, as updated.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For subscription fees and support service settlements to third countries, recommended clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for invoice-based payments, SEPA Credit Transfer for intra-EU payables, and Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit (UCP 600) only if the Spanish SL is the applicant in high-value trade settlements. All outbound disbursements must be matched to an invoice and must indicate the OECD purpose reason code, e.g., 'fees for consulting services' or 'software customisation', and be recorded in the annual Balance of Payments reporting file with Banco de España. The company tax and AML policy must require positive confirmation from the counterparty bank and inclusion of the original invoice reference in the SWIFT instruction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable forwards (maturity up to 12 months)
Non-deliverable forwards referencing EUR/USD with settlement in EUR or USD (for trade-flow based NDF positions subject to bank credit line)
Rolling FX swaps for inventory and subscription revenue transaction cycles
FX spot-forward combinations (par forwards, forward extension legs)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (Cuentas Anuales) deposit in the Mercantile Register, including balance sheet, income statement, statement of changes in equity and notes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil de la provincia del domicilio social (Spanish Mercantile Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after each financial year end; for a 31 December fiscal year, no later than 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit the annual accounts within the legal deadline gives rise to a civil fine from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000; if the filing is not made after two consecutive years the company's registry sheet is closed and the entity loses standing to file any further documents; continued default for three years may trigger administrative cancellation or strike-off proceedings before the Mercantile Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Modelo 200) for the tax period, reflecting taxable profit, credits and definitive self-assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT; Spanish Tax Agency)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the tax year end; for a 31 December year end, by 25 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a surcharge of 5% to 20% plus late-payment interest, with omission penalties ranging from 15% to 150% of the sum involved; a criminal penalty may apply for fraudulent omission above EUR 120,000, but no administrative strike-off consequence arises for tax filings alone.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual information declaration on related-party and non-resident transactions (Modelo 232) where statutory thresholds are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following the filing deadline for Modelo 200; for a 31 December fiscal year, by 25 August of the following year (when applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate filing is penalised at EUR 1,000 per data item or set of omitted items, with a minimum penalty of EUR 2,000 and a maximum of EUR 30,000 per return; administrative strike-off does not apply, but repeated non-compliance may trigger an AEAT audit and enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation or update of ultimate beneficial ownership (Titularidades Reales) in the Central UBO Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro de Titulares Reales under the Consejo General del Notariado
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any shareholding transfer affecting the UBO must be declared within one month of the notarial deed; companies with no change must ensure the registered UBO data remains accurate in the year's corporate maintenance cycle, and a factual update is filed when the annual financial statements are deposited
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-update of UBO information is an infringement under Spanish anti-money-laundering Law 10/2010, subject to monetary penalties up to EUR 150,000 for serious breaches; persistent default may impede dividend distributions, share transfers and the issuance of good-standing certificates, and could result in cancellation of the company's registry standing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit of annual accounts is mandatory for an SL if, for two consecutive fiscal years, it meets at least two of the following thresholds: total assets greater than EUR 2,850,000; net annual turnover greater than EUR 5,700,000; average number of employees greater than 50. Small SLs below these thresholds are exempt from mandatory audit but may opt in for financing or corporate governance reasons.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad) approved by Royal Decree 1514/2007, applied together with the Spanish Commercial Code; listed entities and certain consolidated groups may additionally apply IFRS as endorsed by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must keep an up-to-date register of ultimate beneficial owners in compliance with Law 10/2010. Any transfer of quotas or shares that modifies the UBO must be recorded in the shareholders' ledger and declared to the Registro de Titulares Reales within one month of execution. The annual financial statements deposit acts as the standing confirmation of the company's registers and, in the absence of any ownership change, confirms the continuing accuracy of the existing UBO data; if a transfer occurs, the subsequent notarial deed and registry filing constitute the required annual confirmation for that calendar year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 90 - USD 330 (typical annual registered office / corporate agent fee in Spain)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 4,800 (typical certified audit fee for a small Spanish SL when the audit threshold is met)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: General Spanish corporate income tax rate is 25%. A newly created SL carrying on an economic activity may apply a reduced 15% rate for the first two tax periods with a positive taxable base, provided the entity qualifies as a 'nueva creación' under Ley 27/2014 art. 29. Additional tax benefits include the deduction for reinvestment of extraordinary profits, R&D and technological innovation tax credits up to 42%, and the patent box for IP exploitation income. Spain also allows indefinite carryforward of tax losses; however, the schema template mechanically imposes a 5-year integer for pipeline conformity.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_statutory_note: Under Spanish law (Ley 27/2014, art. 26), tax losses may be carried forward indefinitely. The integer value 5 is supplied solely to match the schema template and should not be read as a Spanish statutory limitation.

corporate_income_tax_regime_notes.institutional_framework: Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS) governed by LEY 27/2014, with regulatory development in RD 634/2015; administered by Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT).
corporate_income_tax_regime_notes.residence_rule: An SL incorporated under Spanish law is resident for tax purposes if it is created in Spain, has its registered office in Spain, or has its effective management (dirección de gestión) in Spain.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 – Declaración del Impuesto sobre Sociedades; filed electronically through the AEAT e-Sede using digital certificate, Cl@ve PIN, or authorized electronic signature.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. An ‘annual’ return is required for each fiscal year of the SL, even if no tax is due. A short period return is required when the SL is newly incorporated or dissolved. Quarterly advanced payments (Modelo ) are separate and outside the final annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed within 25 calendar days following the expiration of the six-month period after the fiscal year-end. For a calendar-year SL, the six-month period ends on 30 June; the final deadline is therefore 25 July of the following year. For a fiscal year ending 30 June, the deadline is 25 January of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIF/NIF of the Spanish SL, legal name, registered address, Spanish fiscal address. This is the entity’s Spanish tax identification number, for example X00000000 or ABC00000000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident shareholder does not use its foreign tax number in this line; the Spanish SL files under its own Spanish NIF. The foreign shareholder data appears on supplementary annexes, not in Box 001.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The precise start and end dates of the fiscal year. For most SLs with a calendar-year accounting period, the entry is 01-01 to 31-12. A newly created SL will state the date of incorporation or commencement of operations as the starting date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ownership does not alter the Spanish fiscal year. The period entered is always the SL’s individual accounting period used for financial statements, not the foreign parent’s fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish taxable base after adjusting the accounting profit for tax adjustments (permanent and timing differences) and compensating prior-year tax losses. This is the amount subject to the 25% tax rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The full Spanish base is taxed at the entity level, regardless of ownership. Non-resident shareholders cannot treat the Spanish SL as a transparent partnership or claim their pro-rata share on their own tax returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The gross income tax quota resulting from applying the applicable tax rate to the taxable base, before deducting tax credits and Bonifications.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The applicable Spanish corporate rate applies to all Spanish income of the SL, whether 100% foreign owned or not. Domestic exemptions or reduced rates must be proved by the SL itself, not by the foreign shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 005 – Cuota diferencial y resultado de la liquidación
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final amount payable after offsets for advanced payments, withholding tax credits, tax credits, and payments made. This line is zero where the SL has applicable losses or sufficient tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder may not use a foreign tax credit on the Spanish Modelo 200. Foreign shareholder tax relief, where any, is separate and is handled by the shareholder’s local jurisdiction; Spanish withholding taxes are recovered or credited in the shareholder’s tax jurisdiction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Modelo 200 constitutes an administrative infraction under Ley General Tributaria (LGT) art. 198. In general, filing after the statutory deadline without prior AEAT requirement triggers a late-payment surcharge of 5% for delay up to 3 months, 10% from 3 to 6 months, 15% from 6 to 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest. Where the omitted amount is not regularized, proportional penalties range from 50% to 125% of the understated tax amount. Fixed penalties also apply for incomplete or incorrect filings and for failure to file an ‘informative’ return.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% (general domestic rate under the Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) regime for dividends paid to non-resident shareholders. Zero is available under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for a qualifying corporate shareholder holding at least 10% for 12 months and meeting non-substance and anti-abuse requirements. A lower treaty rate may apply under Spain’s double tax treaties.)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduction under a double tax treaty or an EU directive, the non-resident shareholder must deliver to the Spanish paying entity a certificate of tax residence (usually Form 01A) issued by the foreign tax authority, evidencing beneficial ownership and the holding period. The Spanish entity must submit Modelo 210 or apply the reduced withholding at source on a properly documented basis. If withholding was made at the statutory 19% and the DTA entitles the shareholder to a lower rate, a refund claim must be filed within the four-year Spanish limitation period using Modelo 210 together with the residence certificate, bank custody document, and a statement of beneficial ownership. Failure to maintain the required documentation defeats the treaty claim.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Spanish domestic withholding for royalty and interest payments to non-residents is 19% for recipients resident in an EU/EEA state that meets information exchange conditions; for residents outside the EU/EEA the general statutory rate is 24%. Under Spanish DTA network, royalty rates are commonly 5% to 10% and interest rates commonly 5% to 10%, depending on the treaty and whether the recipient is the beneficial owner. The same 19% statutory rate may apply where the treaty expressly provides for a reduced rate and the respective certificate of residence is held by the recipient.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 per related party per tax period triggers the obligation to keep Local File documentation; the Master File is required when the consolidated turnover of the group to which the Spanish SL belongs exceeds EUR 75 million, and CbC reporting applies to groups with consolidated turnover above EUR 750 million. In all cases, the documentation must comply with RD 634/2015.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain’s legislation implements the OECD/ATAD anti-abuse framework, requiring a Spanish SL to have actual commercial substance, business purpose, premises, employees, and decision-making functions in relation to activities that give rise to Spanish deductions, transfer pricing positions, or treaty benefits. The SL must avoid pure mailbox or shell status; otherwise, Spanish tax authorities can recharacterize the arrangement, deny treaty or EU-directive benefits, apply the GAAR (LGT art. 15), and require DAC-6 disclosure where a cross-border arrangement offers a tax advantage. Although Spain does not operate an ‘Economic Substance Regulations’ certificate regime in the manner of some offshore jurisdictions, it has a robust economic substance doctrine embedded in the anti-abuse and substance-over-form jurisprudence of the Spanish courts and the General Tax Law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully filing false corporate income tax returns, omitting revenues from customer support and helpdesk subscriptions, using invoices from fictitious suppliers, or manipulating related-party transactions to reduce or eliminate the Spanish taxable base when the amount of tax defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax period (threshold under the Spanish Criminal Code for direct taxes).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under art. 305 of the Criminal Code carries imprisonment from 1 to 5 years and a fine of up to 6 times the defrauded amount. Administrative penalties under LGT art. 191 are proportionally set at 50% to 125% of the underpaid tax, and all lost interest and surcharges are assessed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who commission, approve, or knowingly permit the tax fraud are personally and jointly liable for the tax debt, interest, and sanctions under LGT art. 42.2. In cases of criminal tax evasion, the responsible director can be sentenced to imprisonment, disqualified from holding public positions, receiving subsidies, or acting as a director for a period of 3 to 10 years, and the court may impose a precautionary embargo of personal assets and a travel restriction or surrender of passport pending trial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement Without Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Spanish SL merely as a mailbox entity located at a registered service address with no physical office, no employees, no real economic activity, and no decision-making, while holding customer contracts and financial accounts for the purpose of obtaining treaty benefits or reducing taxation on recurring helpdesk income. Also applicable where the SL is inserted into an artificial chain to channel income to a parent entity that has no substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish tax authorities may disregard or recharacterize the arrangement under the GAAR (LGT art. 15), denying the claimed treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary exemption and recalculating tax at the statutory rate with a 50% surcharge under art. 206 LGT. The uncollectible or diverted income may be reallocated to the substantive corporate entity, with penalties of 50% to 125% of the undue tax advantage. Additionally, the commercial registry and tax authorities can initiate administrative proceedings against the shell structure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a sham SL, being the persons who formally manage or act as legal representatives, may be held personally liable under LGT art. 42 for the amount of tax avoided where they intentionally caused or permitted the substance failure. Where the MLI or DAC-6 rules are implicated, civil liability extends to filing obligations, and directors may face personal fines for failure to disclose reportable arrangements. In aggravated cases, the directors may be prosecuted for illegal tax evasion under art. 310 bis of the Criminal Code.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Anti-Money-Laundering Failures in Payment Processing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving customer subscription payments through Stripe and PayPal without carrying out adequate customer due diligence, implementing no beneficial-ownership verification, failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports in Spain, or using anonymous corporate structures that prevent identification of the true economic owner of the Spanish SL that processes helpdesk fees. Although this activity is Low-Risk under the statutory classification, the deliberate failure to comply with the framework of Law 10/2010 is still an independent infraction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sanctions under Law 10/2010 range from EUR 90,000 to EUR 600,000 for serious infractions and up to EUR 2,000,000 or 3 times the value of the assets for very serious infractions. The competent body (Executive Service of the Commission for the Prevention of Money Laundering and Monetary Infractions) can also impose temporary disqualification, publication of sanctions, and operative restrictions on the entity’s activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives of the SL who knowingly or recklessly neglect AML duties can be personally accountable for unpaid administrative fines. In addition, if the structure is used to launder proceeds, the responsible directors risk criminal prosecution under art. 301 of the Criminal Code, with prison sentences of 6 months to 6 years, a fine, and disqualification from commercial activity; the court may impose preventive measures including asset seizure, surrender of travel documents, and a ban on leaving Spanish territory.
